ActList.description:
`GET /acts` (the company's acts: apply, delete, wake, pause, resume,
and a start per workflow a human may start) and `GET /runs/{run_id}/acts`
(the run's: cancel, and a verdict per gate its workflow has, approved
or not).
ActList.title: ActList

ActRefusal.description:
Why an act would be refused: by policy (`rule` names the rule, as
a 403 would), or by the company's state (`detail` says why, as a 422
would).
ActRefusal.title: ActRefusal

ActView.description:
One act this human could ask for now, by the decision it must win,
with the arguments that decide it; whether it owes a rationale; and
whether it would be allowed — or why not.

A preview, not a decision: it runs the same policy input and the same
state check the act runs, records nothing, and commits nothing. The
act decides again, and is audited. For a start and an apply, whose
refusals also depend on what is sent (the ticket's number, the
blueprint), the preview answers for policy alone.
ActView.title: ActView

ApplyResult.description:
`POST /blueprint/apply`: the CRs created and updated, the
generation this apply made (the one to wait `converged` for), and
the rule the apply was allowed under.
ApplyResult.title: ApplyResult

AuditEventView.description:
One audit row: who acted, through which source, on what, and what
policy answered — with the actor's rationale when the row committed
the company to something. The arguments are never in it.
AuditEventView.title: AuditEventView

BlueprintRequest.description:
`POST /blueprint/preview`, `POST /blueprint/apply`: the blueprint's
YAML text, at most `BLUEPRINT_LIMIT_BYTES` bytes.
BlueprintRequest.title: BlueprintRequest

BlueprintView.description:
`GET /blueprint`: the blueprint's text exactly as a human applied
it — applying it again changes nothing — who applied it and when, and
whether policy enforces it yet: the Company's generation, the one its
phase answers for, and the phase (`activating` until the text applied
is the one policy enforces, `converged` after).
BlueprintView.title: BlueprintView

BoundsView.description:
`GET /company/bounds`: the blueprint's gates and limits as they bind
the company's work, the text every dispatch carries into a
procedure's system prompt.
BoundsView.title: BoundsView

CompanyDeleted.description:
`DELETE /company`: the runs cancelled on the way, and how long the
delete took. The receipt: nothing else of the company is left to
read.
CompanyDeleted.title: CompanyDeleted

CompanyView.description:
`GET /company`: the applied company as its Company CR says —
`activating` until OPA serves its policy, `converged` after; the
generation the phase answers for — its pause, and its limits (null
until the company has converged once).
CompanyView.title: CompanyView

CrewView.description: `GET /runs/{run_id}/crew`: every identity ever bound to the run.
CrewView.title: CrewView

DeleteRequest.description:
`DELETE /company`. The console answers once the company is gone:
its runs ended, its rows swept, its workflow histories deleted.
DeleteRequest.title: DeleteRequest

DocumentView.description:
`GET /documents/{kind}`: one of the company's two documents as it
stands on the base ref, read live through the MCP gateway, clipped to
what a model is shown of it. An absent document is `present: false`,
not an error: a company's first ticks exist to write them.
DocumentView.title: DocumentView

EphemeralAgentView.description:
One ephemeral agent bound to a run: its crew and role, and whether
its identity is still active or was revoked at teardown.
EphemeralAgentView.title: EphemeralAgentView

EventsPage.description:
`GET /events`: the company's rows above the cursor, in id order,
and the cursor to continue from.
EventsPage.title: EventsPage

EventsSpend.description:
The spend to date beside a page of events: the company's, and the
run's when the page is narrowed to one.
EventsSpend.title: EventsSpend

ExecutionView.description:
A workflow's execution as Temporal tells it: its status, and while
it runs, the state its `state()` query answers — a run parked on a
gate reads `parked-<gate>`. `NOT_FOUND` when Temporal knows none.
ExecutionView.title: ExecutionView

Health.description: `GET /healthz`: liveness and the release the console runs.
Health.title: Health

HeartbeatView.description:
`GET /heartbeat`: the standing loop's execution and its ticks since
a fence, oldest first.
HeartbeatView.title: HeartbeatView

LimitsView.description:
The blueprint's caps as they bind the company now, beside what they
are measured against: the per-run cap, the daily cap and today's
spend (since UTC midnight), how many runs may be live at once, and
how long each gate waits for a human before it expires (it escalates
at half).
LimitsView.title: LimitsView

Now.description:
`GET /now`: the registry's clock, the fence a reader takes before
acting and passes back as `?since=`.
Now.title: Now

ParkedView.description:
Where a parked run waits: the gate, since when (its `parked` gate
row), and when nobody answering escalates it (half the deadline) and
expires it. The times are null when the park's row or the gate's
deadline cannot be read.
ParkedView.title: ParkedView

PauseState.description:
`POST /heartbeat/pause`, `POST /heartbeat/resume`: who holds the
loop now, or null once it is resumed.
PauseState.title: PauseState

PauseView.description: Who holds the heartbeat paused, and since when.
PauseView.title: PauseView

PolicyRefusal.description: A 403: policy refused the act, and `rule` names the rule.
PolicyRefusal.title: PolicyRefusal

PreviewResult.description:
`POST /blueprint/preview`: what applying the blueprint would
change, against what the cluster hosts. Nothing is written.
PreviewResult.title: PreviewResult

Problem.description:
Why a request was not answered: 401 (no verified human), 404 (no
company is applied), 422 (it names something that cannot be acted
on, or a body that does not validate), 503 (Temporal unreachable).
Problem.title: Problem

RunCancelled.description:
`POST /runs/{run_id}/cancel`: the workflow was asked to stop; its
teardown compensates.
RunCancelled.title: RunCancelled

RunDetail.description: `GET /runs/{run_id}`: the record and its workflow's execution.
RunDetail.title: RunDetail

RunList.description:
`GET /runs`: the company's runs, oldest first; with `?state=parked`,
only those parked on a gate.
RunList.title: RunList

RunSpendView.description: `GET /runs/{run_id}/spend`: the run's total and every call behind it.
RunSpendView.title: RunSpendView

RunStarted.description:
`POST /runs`: the run id and the workflow addressing it. The run's
record appears a moment later, when the worker writes it.
RunStarted.title: RunStarted

RunView.description:
One run's record: its task, status and what it delivered, and the
gate it is parked on, if any (null for a run that is not).
RunView.title: RunView

SpendEntryView.description: One model call in the ledger, attributed.
SpendEntryView.title: SpendEntryView

SpendView.description: `GET /spend`: the company's spend and tokens since a fence.
SpendView.title: SpendView

StandingAgentView.description:
One standing agent: its hire's name, its catalog role, whether the
reconciler converged it, and whether it is the conductor the
company's runs are requested under.
StandingAgentView.title: StandingAgentView

StartRunRequest.description:
`POST /runs`: a run on a ticket (`implement`) or a pull request
(`review`), by its number on the company repository.
StartRunRequest.title: StartRunRequest

StoryView.description: `GET /runs/{run_id}/story`: the run's rows in order, every source.
StoryView.title: StoryView

TickView.description: One heartbeat tick: what it ended on and why.
TickView.title: TickView

TicketList.description:
`GET /tickets`: every ticket the company filed on its repository,
ascending by number — the ones its agents and the platform filed,
whatever the git host says of them since.
TicketList.title: TicketList

TicketView.description:
One ticket the company filed: its number on the repository, the
run that filed it, when.
TicketView.title: TicketView

VerdictRecorded.description:
`POST /runs/{run_id}/gates/{gate}`: the verdict recorded under the
human's name, and delivered.
VerdictRecorded.title: VerdictRecorded

WhoAmI.description:
`GET /whoami`: the verified human, and the company the cluster
hosts (none before the first apply).
WhoAmI.title: WhoAmI

Woken.description: `POST /heartbeat/wake`: the loop was nudged to look now.
Woken.title: Woken

info.description: The console interface: the one way a person acts on a company and reads it. Every act is decided by policy and audited under the human's name.
info.title: poseidon-console
